subject.description: The subject in a few words.

audience.description: Who it is written for: starting level and kind of goal. No personal details.

language.description: BCP 47 language tag of the content.

why.description: One sentence on why this module matters for the course goal.

keyIdeas.description: The few ideas the learner must leave with.

belief.description: The wrong idea, stated as a learner would believe it.

correction.description: What is actually true, and why the wrong idea is tempting.

sign.description: How it shows up in an answer.

blocks.description: The script, in teaching order. The tutor adapts delivery to the learner.

type.description: Optional: a block without a type is Markdown.

body.description: Markdown. For practice and recall blocks, the framing around the check.

checkId.description: For practice and recall: the check this block puts to the learner.

kind.description: flowchart = steps and decisions; sequence = messages between actors over time; concept = ideas and how they relate.

source.description: Mermaid source: `flowchart TD` / `flowchart LR` for flowchart and concept maps, `sequenceDiagram` for sequence. Plain labels only: no HTML, no click handlers, no styling directives.

description.description: What the diagram shows, in plain sentences. Read by screen readers, and shown instead of the diagram if it cannot be drawn.

code.description: The code, as it should appear. Under about 40 lines.

caption.description: One or two sentences on what to notice.

runnable.description: JavaScript only: the learner may press Run to see its console output, in a sandbox with no network and a time limit.

prompt.description: Markdown: what to put in order, and by what (time, size, the steps of a procedure).

items.description: The items IN THE CORRECT ORDER. The learner sees them shuffled.

explanation.description: Why this is the order. Shown with the result.

hints.description: Up to three hints from gentle to pointed. A hint guides thinking and never states the answer.

prompt.description: Markdown: what to match with what.

pairs.description: The correct pairs. The learner sees the right-hand items shuffled.

distractors.description: Extra right-hand items that match nothing.

hints.description: Up to three hints from gentle to pointed. A hint guides thinking and never states the answer.

mode.description: code shows the text in a monospace font and compares answers case-sensitively.

text.description: The sentence or code with each gap written as {{1}}, {{2}} and so on, in order.

accept.description: Every answer that counts as right. The first is the one shown after answering.

caseSensitive.description: Defaults to false in prose and true in code.

hints.description: Up to three hints from gentle to pointed. A hint guides thinking and never states the answer.

prompt.description: Markdown: the problem the worked example solves.

text.description: Markdown: this step of the solution and why it is taken.

predict.description: A question the learner answers before this step is revealed, such as 'What would you do next?'. Graded against the step's text.

front.description: Markdown: a question that forces recall.

columns.description: Column headings. The first heads the row labels.

rows.description: One per thing compared; cells follow the columns after the first.

tone.description: tip = a useful shortcut; warning = a real hazard; key-idea = the one thing to remember; common-mistake = what learners often get wrong, and the fix.

body.description: Markdown, a few sentences at most.

image.description: The id of a find_images result. Never made up.

alt.description: What the picture shows, for someone who cannot see it. Specific, one or two sentences; never just a file name.

caption.description: Shown under this picture: what to notice.

credit.description: Filled in by the engine from the search result; leave it out.

title.description: The file's title at the source.

licence.description: Short licence name, such as "CC BY-SA 4.0" or "Public domain".

sourceUrl.description: The file's page at the source, where its full licence and history are.

images.description: One picture, or up to six shown side by side to compare (the cards of a suit, leaf shapes).

caption.description: Under the whole block: what to look at and why it matters.

kind.description: choice = multiple choice; short = a few words or one sentence; explain = in their own words; numeric = a number.

prompt.description: Markdown shown to the learner: only the question, self-contained.

options.description: For choice only. Distractors should be what real misconceptions produce.

correctOption.description: For choice only: zero-based index of the right option.

optionMisconceptions.description: For choice only: per option, the misconception id that picking it reveals, or null.

tolerance.description: For numeric only: accepted absolute error.

answerKey.description: The complete correct answer. Stays in the engine until the learner has answered.

rubric.description: For short and explain: what full and partial credit need.

hints.description: Up to three hints from gentle to pointed. A hint guides thinking and never states the answer.

misconceptionIds.description: Misconceptions of this objective that this check can reveal.

review.description: Facts worth spaced review once met.

brief.description: Markdown: what to build or do, and why it matters.
